duplicateMapping.comparison: Distinct from accepted 9c138e4d rational proof and 3135a43b auxiliary work: the whole guided geometry-to-half-angle-to-equation chain is retained.

results.difficultyReason: Use the supplied similar triangles and unit-circle coordinates, connect an isosceles angle to a half-angle tangent identity, then solve on the stated interval.
results.sourceDomainAndAnswerDisposition: NT=1-sin theta, TQ=cos theta, NS=2, hence SP=2cos theta/(1-sin theta); rationalisation gives sec theta+tan theta. The isosceles angle is pi/4+theta/2, and its tangent equals SP/2. Since this angle lies in (0,pi/2), its tangent equals sqrt(3) only at pi/3, so theta=pi/6. The TikZ preserves the original circle, labelled N,Q,T,S,P, secant, horizontal TQ, y=-1 and angle relationships.
